reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates that nanoscale compositional fluctuations exist in HEAs and can influence mechanical behavior, but neither passage provides any support for the key premises that quantitative TEM/EDS descriptors can be extracted to predict bulk tensile properties or that an ML surrogate would achieve the claimed accuracy/efficiency gains. The evidence is only loosely related to the specific methodological claims.
premises: TEM/EDS can extract quantitative microstructural descriptors (fluctuation amplitude, correlation lengths) of hierarchical chemical heterogeneity in HfNbTiVAl10
These descriptors mediate the relationship between microstructure and mechanical properties (Young's modulus, yield strength, fracture toughness)
A physics-informed ML model using these descriptors can bypass full-scale simulations (CALPHAD, first-principles) and predict properties with 10-15% error reduction
The approach yields an order-of-magnitude reduction in computational demand
